senses.gloss: स्मित- + पूर्व स्मित- + पूर्व, adv. smiling first.
स्मित- + शोभिन् स्मित- + शोभिन् (vb. स्मि), adj., f. नी, smiling beautifully, Lass. 2. ed. 55, 66.
† श्मील् श्मील्, स्मील् स्मील् (cf. मील्), i. 1, Par. To wink, to contract the eyelids.

स्मि स्मि, i. 1, Ātm. (in epic poetry also Par., Chr. 27, 1), To smile, Chr. 27, 3. स्मित,
 1. Smiling, Pañc. i. d. 152.
 2. Blown (as a flower), Pañc. i. d. 152. n. A smile, Vikr. 13, 4.
 --Comp.
 --† i. 10, Ātm. To despise. Frequent. सेष्मीय, To suffer from convulsions, to tremble, Mālav. 47, 5.
 --With अभि अभि, To smile, MBh. 3, 8237.
 --With उद् उद्, To smile, MBh. 1, 7059. उत्स्मायित्वा (Rām. 1, 1, 63), is an anomalous form either for उत्स्माययित्वा, Caus. ‘To make a mock of, to insult.’ or for उत्स्मित्वा, and then to be changed to उत्स्मयित्वा, ‘To burst into laughter.’
 --With अभ्युद् अभि-उद्, To smile, Chr. 44, 35.
 --With वि वि,
 1. To be surprised, Rām. 3, 49, 3.
 2. To admire.
 3. To be proud, Man. 4, 236. विस्मित, Astonished, perplexed, Hit. 56, 18.
 --Comp.
 --Caus. स्मापय, To cause to be surprised, Ragh. 2, 33.
 --Cf. स्मेर and O.H.G. smielan; A.S. smaerc, smirk; [] Lat. mirari; probably σμοιός, μέμϕομαι (Caus.), μῶμος.

† स्मिट् स्मिट् (akin to स्मि), i. 10, Par.
 1. To despise.
 2. To love.
 3. To go.
